cutoff_window.basis: Local repository automation run time; only public web sources with visible publication, submission, or update evidence inside this window were included.

federation_boundary.local_scope: AI-assisted development practice implications, including context architecture, source workflows, guidance structure, agent operating practices, coding practices, retrieval and tool governance, verification, risk controls, and adoption patterns.

qualifying_findings.title: Desktop coding agents move into broad individual access
qualifying_findings.date_evidence: GitHub changelog page shows July 7, 2026 at the article header.
qualifying_findings.summary: GitHub made the Copilot app available on every Copilot plan across macOS, Windows, and Linux, with BYOK support and an organization or enterprise policy dependency for Business and Enterprise access.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: Agent-driven development is shifting from enterprise-only or preview workflows into default desktop access, so local adoption guidance should treat onboarding, plan boundaries, BYOK policy, and admin enablement as first-class operating model concerns.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Keep local notes focused on desktop-agent rollout gates, BYOK governance, and plan-aware team onboarding rather than duplicating Copilot product coverage.
follow_up_notes: During ingest, compare with adoption and operating model pages that describe coding-agent onboarding and admin enablement.
Route product availability details to the upstream AI wiki if durable product coverage is needed.

qualifying_findings.title: Per-user AI credit budgets become admin-facing controls
qualifying_findings.date_evidence: GitHub changelog page shows July 7, 2026 at the article header.
qualifying_findings.summary: GitHub Enterprise Cloud administrators can create cost-center user-level budgets directly in the billing UI, assign teams or users to cost centers, and keep coverage synchronized as membership changes.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: AI-assisted development governance increasingly includes per-user spend controls that follow team membership, which turns cost management into an operational guardrail rather than a separate finance report.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Governance pages should distinguish access control, spend control, usage reporting, and budget drift as separate adoption controls for coding-agent programs.
follow_up_notes: During ingest, check whether existing spend-control notes mention per-user budgets as a governed team boundary.
Do not duplicate GitHub billing-product documentation locally.

qualifying_findings.title: Copilot spend visibility consolidates into built-in billing surfaces
qualifying_findings.date_evidence: GitHub changelog page shows July 7, 2026 at the article header.
qualifying_findings.summary: GitHub announced that the Copilot Billing Preview app will retire on August 3, 2026, and directed teams to built-in billing settings, budgets, user-level budgets, usage reports, and the billing API for spend visibility.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: AI coding spend governance is moving toward integrated billing APIs and native admin settings, which should reduce reliance on temporary sidecar reporting tools and support repeatable audit workflows.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Local governance guidance should prefer durable billing and usage APIs for evidence collection, while noting that preview reporting surfaces may disappear.
follow_up_notes: During ingest, align with audit-log and spend-control pages if they mention preview billing surfaces.
Route product retirement facts upstream if product lifecycle coverage is needed.

qualifying_findings.title: Sandbox observability exposes per-session agent workload cost
qualifying_findings.date_evidence: Vercel changelog page shows 7 Jul 2026 at the article header.
qualifying_findings.summary: Vercel Sandbox observability now reports resource metrics such as active CPU, provisioned memory, data transfer, running sandboxes, and sessions, grouped by Sandbox Name and Sandbox Session ID and available through dashboard and CLI queries.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: Agent workloads that create sandboxes at scale need cost and resource telemetry tied to each sandbox session, so verification environments can be right-sized and anomalous package downloads or network usage can be investigated.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Harness and preview-environment pages should treat sandbox resource metrics, session IDs, and CLI-accessible usage data as evidence for agent evaluation and cost control.
follow_up_notes: During ingest, compare against existing harness architecture and remote-agent proof-gate notes.
Keep Vercel product capability detail upstream-owned; retain the local implication about sandbox telemetry as verification evidence.

qualifying_findings.title: Tool-use evaluation separates skipped, ignored, fabricated, and unnecessary calls
qualifying_findings.date_evidence: arXiv abstract page shows Submitted on 6 Jul 2026 and submission history v1 Mon, 6 Jul 2026 05:25:21 UTC.
qualifying_findings.summary: ToolFailBench proposes a diagnostic benchmark for tool-use failures across 1,000 tasks and labels traces with categories such as Tool-Skip, Result-Ignore, Output-Fabrication, and Unnecessary-Tool-Use, showing that similar aggregate scores can hide distinct tool-use failure modes.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: AI-assisted development evals should not stop at final-answer or patch success; they should classify whether a coding agent called the needed tool, used the result, fabricated output, or called tools unnecessarily.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Local verification pages should consider trace-level tool-use taxonomies for coding-agent checks, especially when MCP or CLI calls are required for correctness.
follow_up_notes: During ingest, route benchmark and model background upstream; keep local synthesis about diagnostic categories for tool-call practice.
Compare with tool-call practice and MCP governance leaves.

qualifying_findings.title: Repository process logs can derive project-specific agent roles
qualifying_findings.date_evidence: arXiv abstract page shows Submitted on 6 Jul 2026 and submission history v1 Mon, 6 Jul 2026 11:22:25 UTC.
qualifying_findings.summary: A BPM 2026 paper proposes using object-centric, imperative, and declarative process mining on software repository event logs to discover project-specific AI agent roles and generate matching agent specifications and implementations.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: Subagent and workflow design can be grounded in observed repository processes instead of only generic role templates, but the approach also raises questions about granularity, coordination overhead, and validation against human expectations.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Agent-workflow guidance should distinguish generic subagent role packs from repo-derived agent specifications that reflect actual source workflow evidence.
follow_up_notes: During ingest, compare with local subagent planning and coordinator-worker workflow pages.
Record caveats about using repository logs without exposing private or sensitive process data.

qualifying_findings.title: Concurrent agent-authored PRs create measurable merge-conflict risk
qualifying_findings.visible_date: Submitted on 6 Jul 2026; last revised 7 Jul 2026
qualifying_findings.date_evidence: arXiv abstract page shows Submitted on 6 Jul 2026, last revised 7 Jul 2026, with v2 Tue, 7 Jul 2026 02:40:06 UTC.
qualifying_findings.summary: The paper analyzes AI agent pull requests and reports that exact temporal overlap appears in 40.2 percent of repositories, co-active pairs account for 79.4 percent of agent PRs, and cross-agent pairs have higher textual conflict rates than intra-agent pairs in sampled replayed merges.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: Parallel coding agents need source-workflow controls for worktree isolation, branch coordination, PR scheduling, merge ownership, and conflict review because ordinary git conflict detection may miss intent-level collisions.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Source workflow pages should treat multi-agent concurrency as a managed queue and coordination problem, not only as independent PR generation.
follow_up_notes: During ingest, compare with worktree-isolated parallel agent and source-branching practice leaves.
Route dataset background upstream if the AI wiki owns durable AIDev coverage.

qualifying_findings.title: Coding-agent hidden states encode current and future program outcomes
qualifying_findings.date_evidence: arXiv abstract page shows Submitted on 6 Jul 2026 and submission history v1 Mon, 6 Jul 2026 15:08:26 UTC.
qualifying_findings.summary: The Latent Programming Horizons paper reports that probes over model residual streams can decode whether evolving code parses, passes tests, reduces failing tests, or introduces regressions, and can predict future edit outcomes above chance roughly 25 steps ahead.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: Verification research may eventually inspect internal agent-state signals for parse, test, and regression risk, but current local practice should treat this as research evidence rather than deployable assurance.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Verification pages can mention internal-state probing as an emerging evaluation direction while keeping steady-state practice anchored in observable tests, builds, traces, and review gates.
follow_up_notes: During ingest, preserve uncertainty and avoid presenting latent-horizon probes as a production control.
Compare with regression detection and evaluation architecture leaves.

qualifying_findings.title: Compilable vulnerability benchmarks expose weak localization by agentic setups
qualifying_findings.date_evidence: arXiv abstract page shows Submitted on 6 Jul 2026 and submission history v1 Mon, 6 Jul 2026 07:02:56 UTC.
qualifying_findings.summary: RustMizan introduces a compilable, contamination-aware Rust vulnerability benchmark with crate, file, and function-level variants; in an agentic command-line setup, binary classification scores remain moderate while line localization F1 stays near 20 percent and drops under adversarial cues.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters: Security-oriented AI code review and vulnerability checks need compilable fixtures, contamination controls, and localization metrics, because broad vulnerability labels can hide weak line-level evidence.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: AI code review checklists should separate vulnerability classification from localization, proof quality, compilation context, and contamination-aware evaluation.
follow_up_notes: During ingest, compare with AI code review and security-evaluation pages.
Route Rust and benchmark background upstream if durable entity coverage is needed.
